correctness.rationale: For every finite G-set, any semigroup inner inverse restricts to an equivariant section on the image. On each transitive image orbit that section must land isomorphically in a same-type source orbit. This exact criterion yields a support-wise inclusion-exclusion product and a constructive iff condition for every equivariant map to be regular. Boundary cases and the full semigroup criterion were tested by an independent point-level program in ten finite group actions, including nonabelian S3. Finite tests corroborate but do not establish universal validity.

originality.rationale: The finite-G-set relative-rank paper supplies orbit-map facts, not an exact von Neumann regular rank polynomial. The 2025 total-cardinality and Green-relations papers also do not state the section-sieve enumeration or the iff criterion for a wholly regular monoid. Projective/free group-act work has a narrower domain. Searches of indexed mathematical findings and published sources did not expose a theorem logically covering both claims; historical priority remains conditional on inaccessible/unindexed prior work.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete image-cardinality classification of a natural nontrivial semigroup-theoretic subset, for all finite groups and arbitrary finite actions. It also yields an iff group-action criterion for regularity of the whole endomorphism monoid. The example of a C2-action with two fixed points and one free orbit (14 regular among 16 maps) proves the statistic is not equivalent to total counts. The exact connection to tables of marks makes the result reproducible and useful for concrete equivariant monoids.
